findings.title: Materials' 54-point lens gap signals collapse
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.02x forward but 37.02x trailing, a 54-point percentile gap — the widest in the table. Analysts are underwriting 118 percent earnings growth, which would be the steepest rebound of any sector, yet the trailing multiple still sits at the 88th percentile of its five-year range.

findings.title: Health Care at 100th percentile forward, 80th trailing
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple has hit the richest percentile of its five-year range while its trailing multiple sits at just the 80th. The 43 percent compression between lenses implies analysts expect 77 percent earnings growth, a bet that the sector's reported earnings will catch up to an already-extreme valuation.

findings.title: Information Technology's forward percentile collapses to zero
findings.body: Information Technology's forward P/E percentile has fallen to 0 — the cheapest it has been in five years — even though its trailing multiple is at the 25th percentile. The 39 percent compression between lenses implies 64 percent expected earnings growth, meaning the market is pricing in a surge in profits that has not yet shown up in reported results.
